summary.headline: Shree Cement Q2 FY27 India volumes rose 18% YoY to 9.31 mt, but consol EBITDA/ton fell to INR966 on higher fuel cost.
summary.overview: India sales volume grew about 18% YoY to 9.31 million tonnes, with realisation up 1% to INR4,870 per tonne. Consolidated EBITDA rose about 4% YoY to INR1,016 crore, but EBITDA per tonne fell to INR966 from INR1,055, mainly due to higher fuel cost (landed cost INR2.09 per kcal vs INR1.66 a year ago). Sequentially, volumes fell 11% in India and consolidated EBITDA dropped from INR1,272 crore on seasonality, West Asia conflict and weak monsoon. Management reiterated 40-41 million tonne India volume guidance for FY27 and an 80 million tonne capacity target.

segments.name: India cement
segments.commentary: Volumes 9.31 mt (+18% YoY); capacity utilisation 56% vs 52% a year ago. Realisation INR4,870 per tonne. South grew fastest, followed by North and then East, per management.

segments.name: UAE (Union Cement, step-down subsidiary)
segments.commentary: New 3 mt cement mill commissioned in September 2026, taking capacity to 7 mtpa. H1 FY27 volume about 2.1 mt; management expects similar H2 run-rate and about 4-5 mt annualised after the new mill ramps (about 30% utilisation in first year).

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete
segments.commentary: 28 commercial plants plus captive units, 35 plants in total. Volume 2.73 lakh cubic metres (+153% YoY), revenue INR129 crore (+182% YoY), EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Total power capacity about 1,170 MW: 503 MW thermal and 667 MW green (WHR, solar, wind). Green power was 65.2% of electricity consumption in Q2. Around 80 MW of additional renewable capacity in progress. External power sales not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India volume guidance of 40-41 million tonnes; management said it could reach up to 41 mt.
Q3 landed fuel cost guided at about INR2.15-2.20 per kcal (vs INR2.09 in Q2); CFO also cited around INR2.20.
Q3 cost expected to be broadly similar to Q2 per management; bag and other external costs hard to forecast.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 performance reasonably better, if not similar, to Q2.
Capex guided at INR700-800 crore for H2 FY27.
Meghalaya greenfield integrated plant expected to commission in the quarter ending 31 March 2028.
Target to reach 80 million tonnes capacity in the short term; commitment to grow slightly faster than industry.
Working capital: clinker inventory build of about INR100 crore expected to be consumed; sustainable inventory change INR60-70 crore by year-end.
Premium share internal target above 40% within a few years.
capex_capacity: Meghalaya greenfield integrated plant: construction mobilised, contractors and orders placed; commissioning now targeted for the quarter ending 31 March 2028 after state government hearing cleared doubts.
UAE: new 3 mt cement mill commissioned in September 2026; total UAE capacity 7 mtpa.
India capacity about 70 mt per management; utilisation 56% in Q2.
Green power capacity 667 MW with about 80 MW more under implementation.
Alternate fuel/TSR rose from about 2% to about 5%; more plants being commissioned for AFR handling.
demand_pricing: Industry demand growth estimated at 7-10% in Q2 per management, with weak monsoon hitting rural demand; infrastructure, railways, housing and data centres supporting demand.
Prices improved in October vs September per management; industry reports of INR20-25 per bag hikes in North and East referenced by an analyst.
Premium cement sells INR25-35 per bag above base; newer premium brands (Total, Marble) about INR35-40 higher.
Non-trade share rising due to institutional and infrastructure projects; management says trade remains core.
Blended cement share about 58% vs 68% a year ago; pet coke fell to about 11% of fuel mix from 66%, imported coal 75%.
Freight cost per tonne fell sharply in Q2 due to lower run-to-market, lean-season railway discounts and data-based freight fixation; management says no one-offs but may not be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: What was landed fuel cost per kcal and outlook for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 landed cost INR2.09 vs INR1.66 a year ago and INR1.95 in Q1; Q3 guided at about INR2.15-2.20 based on order pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 volume growth and industry demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand triggers are strong; industry growth 7-10% in Q2; Shree expects to grow slightly better than industry if demand holds at around 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Blended cost of production and pure cement cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended cost INR4,636 per tonne vs INR4,245 YoY and INR4,329 QoQ; pure cement cost not available, to be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Freight cost drop and whether one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by lower run-to-market, lean-season railway discounts and data-based freight fixation; management said there is no one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Trade vs non-trade mix and Meghalaya status?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade 61%, balance non-trade; Meghalaya protests cleared by state government, workforce and contractors mobilised, commissioning in FY28 still targeted.

qa_highlights.question: UAE volume outlook after new 3 mt mill?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 UAE volume about 2.1 mt; H2 similar; annualised UAE total about 4-5 mt after new capacity ramps (about 30% of 3 mt taken in first year).

risks_watch: Weak monsoon could delay rural cement demand recovery in H2.
Fuel cost: Q3 landed cost guided up to INR2.20 per kcal; pet coke to imported coal shift and alternative fuel ramp-up need monitoring.
Freight savings in Q2 may not be sustained beyond lean season, per management.
West Asia conflict affecting UAE demand; new UAE mill ramp-up typically takes 2-3 years.
Meghalaya plant execution after local protests; commissioning date Q4 FY28 (March 2028 quarter).
Receivables up about INR300 crore QoQ, contributing to working capital pressure.
Packaging/bag cost and other external costs described as rapidly moving and hard to forecast.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, pricing and premium mix, with a clear 40-41 mt FY27 guide. Cautious and evasive on granular disclosures: clinker volumes, UAE revenue and EBITDA, power external sales and pure cement cost were withheld, and cost outlook was qualified as hard to forecast.
key_quotes: If this trend continues, then what we have promised you all that our growth will be slightly better than the industry.
Trade has been our bread and butter. So trade, we will be pushing.
What I say is the most efficient producer. That is our core DNA that we'll continue to push.
So we have gradually reduced the use of pet coke because of the increased prices.

growth.why: FY27 India volume guided at 40-41 Mt (reiterated), backed by 56% utilisation and UAE 3 mt mill commissioned Sept 2026, with Meghalaya greenfield plant slated for quarter ending 31 Mar 2028; Q2 India volumes +18% YoY and consolidated EBITDA +4% YoY, but Q3 fuel cost guided higher at INR2.15-2.20/kcal.
